Reviewer Expertise:

Epidemiology

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to confirm that it is of an acceptable scientific standard.

The study result showing that the Tanzania regions which have high level of food production but associated with high stunting is an indication of lack of access to food. That is, the inability to purchase available food or consume other varieties of food. The implication is the need to improve access to food by improving household income and also the need to educate the people on food utilisation.

Under the "Stunting and average monthly household food consumption expenditure" subheading, there is an incorrect statement as the negative correlation value should be interpreted as: "the higher the average monthly household food consumption expenditure, the lower is the prevalence of stunting". The paper contain other typos that need to be corrected.

In addition, the negative correlation between the prevalence of stunting and household food consumption reinforces the importance of food accessibility or the affordability of food. As evidenced in the literature, peasant farmers often depend on their own production for household food consumption and they lack the means to afford other varieties of foods not produced. Conclusively, consistent food production addresses one dimension (availability) of food security. There is need for other dimensions (accessibility, utilisation and stability) to be improved.

Agricultural production economics, agricultural finance,  food security, gender studies, climate impacts on agriculture and adaptation.

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to confirm that it is of an acceptable scientific standard, however I have significant reservations, as outlined above.

Thank you for carefully addressing the previous comments. I appreciate that the revised manuscript now clearly specifies the regional names (e.g., Njombe), which substantially improves the transparency and interpretability of the findings. This clarification strengthens the ecological comparisons presented in the study.

I would like to offer one additional suggestion to further enhance clarity in the abstract and to minimize potential ambiguity.

In particular, the sentence:

“It was further found that some regions which have higher levels of stunting such as Njombe, have the lowest level of basic need poverty.”

may be somewhat difficult for readers to interpret unambiguously. The phrase “lowest level of basic need poverty” could be open to different interpretations, as it is not immediately clear whether this refers to poverty depth, poverty severity, or poverty rate.

As “basic needs poverty” appears to represent the proportion of households unable to meet minimum consumption needs, it may improve clarity to explicitly refer to “poverty rates.” For example, the sentence could be revised as follows:

“Furthermore, some regions with high stunting prevalence (e.g., Njombe) were found to have relatively low basic-needs poverty rates.”

This wording more directly conveys the paradoxical pattern described in the title — namely, that regions with higher stunting do not necessarily correspond to regions with higher poverty rates — and would help readers more readily grasp the conceptual contrast highlighted in the study.

Clarifying this expression would further strengthen the internal consistency between the title (“paradox”), the reported results, and their interpretation in the abstract.

In addition, Figure 5 should ideally be self-explanatory without requiring reference to the main text. I would recommend adding a brief note in the figure legend clarifying the meaning of the blue squares and pink circles to improve readability.

Overall, the manuscript has improved substantially, and with minor clarifications to wording and figure presentation, it will provide a clearer and more compelling account of the ecological paradox described.

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to confirm that it is of an acceptable scientific standard.

Despite the need for epidemiological studies targeting developing countries, there are still few publications. In this context, an ecological study design that allows low-cost analysis would be beneficial. I read this paper with great interest.

Ecological studies cannot prove causality, but the author should choose appropriate parameters to clarify the relationship with the prevalence of stunting. The author describes it as a paradox that the food production value is positively correlated with stunting, but the indicators observed are not appropriate. The author should observe in more detail what food groups are produced. For example, the production of coffee beans would not be directly related to an increase in nutrient intake.

Furthermore, for mothers in Region Njombe, the author should show statistical data on longer hours of work in comparison with other areas.

In Figures 1-3: 
                The graphs presenting the 26 regions should show approximate equations. In addition, for those regions that had large residuals from the equation, the reasons should be discussed.
                    The figures should be drawn squares with numbers like [1], [2] - [26], indicating the name of the region, rather than a square black box, so that the stunting situation and economic situation in Tanzania can be understood. Since most of the readers have unknown area names in Tanzania, I suppose that as possible as simple maps should be shown with transport infrastructure (road network or ocean ports). In this peer review, I was able to get some Tanzania information by the administrative regions of Tanzania map (referred 
                Tanzania National Nutrition Survey 2018.pdf, page 7, Figure 1), or the Tanzania transport map (website:
                https://www.tanzaniainvest.com/transport ). The figures of present paper did not provide enough information about regions in Tanzania.

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to confirm that it is of an acceptable scientific standard, however I have significant reservations, as outlined above.

Commendation:

I would like to commend the authors for coming up with this paper in which they have attempted to provide some answers about the paradox relationship between food production, stunting, expenditure, and poverty in Tanzania. They have correctly pointed out that high food producing regions are also leading in the prevalence of stunting.

Suggestion: change the title to read “the paradox of food production, expenditure, poverty, and stunting in Tanzania….” To reflect what is described in the paper.

Methodology: 
                Sampling procedure for the Household Budget Survey and Tanzania National Nutrition Survey has been described but not for the agriculture statistics. The authors should explain how the data on agriculture production is collected. It would also be useful to indicate when these various surveys were carried out (date and month). This information has implications on the relationships of the variables and therefore interpretation of the results.
                    Provide the definition of average consumption. The household budget survey presents proportion of food and non-food expenditures, it would be more logical to look into these categories and assess how they relate to stunting instead of just looking at the average expenditure and expenditure on food only. In addition, what are the kinds of foods that are accessed by households? Do they add to the diversity of nutritious foods? 
                Results: 
                Add lines of fit on the correlation graphs (scatter plots) to assist the reader to get a clear picture of the relationship between the variables.
                    Stunting and average monthly household consumption expenditure (AMHCE): the authors have stated that there was a significant negative relationship between stunting and AMHCE; but explained that as AMCHE increased, stunting also increased. Is this the meaning of a negative relationship? This area needs clarification.
                    Stunting and AMHFCE: authors observed a negative relationship, but did not elaborate further on this relationship the way they have done for other relationships. There is a need for consistency.
                    Stunting and basic need poverty: what is the basis of selecting only eight regions. It is better to present data for all regions to give the reader a full perspective of the data you have analysed and single out the eight regions in the description of the results. In the current analysis, the Njombe region should appear in both figures 4 and 5. However, it would also be interesting to identify regions that appear in both figures 4&5.
                    It would also be more informative to present data on the relationship between stunting and monthly food and non food expenditures to show how the two types of expenditure contribute to stunting. Nevertheless, this is not a very strong indicator since it does not tell us what types of foods are purchased and consumed by children. 
                Discussion 
                “This indicates that food security may not entail nutrition security” This is a statement in the discussion, but not explained fully. Authors should be cautious when using these terminologies. In this particular study, they assessed the relationship between food production or availability and stunting and not food security, which has four pillars. It would be better to say that 
                            food availability may not entail food consumption and related outcomes; rather than using words such as food and nutrition security, which were not assessed in this study.
                    Page 7 para 3 is more speculative and not supported by the available data. It should be revised to provide more information about expenditure and what kinds of foods are purchased and actually fed to children. It would also be more logical to consider other variables such as minimum acceptable diet (MAD) for children and household dietary diversity score (HDDS).

February 2023? It is now January 2026? Why such a gap?

Introduction

Methods

What was the explicit Booleen phrase(s) used for the search?

20 articles, since the databases were started? AS I don’t see a specific data range, this raises concerns of how to draw meaningful conclusions from such date dispersed literature as the phenomenon in question is dynamic and has changed drastically over recent years. A greater detail and defense of the choice made here need to be elaborated upon.

Results

Having a table listing all 20 articles with some broad details, is just descriptive and take 4 whole pages. The table should be a summary if it is retained, with this large table being in the appendix as it adds very little to the study.

Much of this appears to be descriptive and adds little to the body of knowledge.

Discussion

This is the opportunity to show what you paper is contributing but it is very lacking in interpretation.

The Discussion section should begin with a general discussion putting what the results mean in general language and this should be linked back to the prior literature, identifying where other authors have agreed or disagreed with your findings. Effectively summating what is different or the same about your findings for your specific study in Peru.

Next should be Theoretical Contributions, I would recommend looking at Homer, S. T., & Lim, W. M. (2024). Theory development in a globalized world: Bridging “doing as the romans do” with “understanding why the romans do it”. Global Business and Organizational Excellence, 43(3), 127-138. This will help you position your study and how you can develop the theory, which should be introduced what theory is underpinning the study in the literature review, hence the importance when highlight a conceptual or theoretical model.

Thus, it is important to set a clear context of the messo level of Peru and what makes it unique, so you can add to the theory around a specific scope. Thus, rather than trying to add to the generalizable theory, you add your own small specific piece which many have unique elements that disagree with the core theory. What from the Peruvian perspective is USR? You can construct a model from your findings here

Following this, should be Practical Recommendations, here you should discuss why practitioners should want to take note of and how they can actually implement this within their specific universities within Peru, and then what perhaps is missing or different from the international context. The more specific the better, so that the application is tangible. What is the potential? This may also link to the university ranking systems such as the sustainability rankings in QS and THE.

This could be followed by Policy Recommendations, both at the organisational level of the universities and at the governmental level, what policies would encourage the implementation of your findings and how would it be of benefit? Of course, this would follow on from what the practical implications are that you have defined.

Conclusion

Structure here seems fine but will need to be updated inline with changes throughout the manuscript.

The topic is promising but needs extensive reworking to ensure the contribution to the literature is captured.

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to state that I do not consider it to be of an acceptable scientific standard, for reasons outlined above.

I have reviewed your manuscript with great interest. The topic addressed is relevant and timely, as University Social Responsibility (USR) is a strategic axis for higher education, particularly in Latin America. The work integrates studies in both Spanish and English, follows PRISMA guidelines, and combines legislative, institutional, and empirical perspectives. These aspects, together with the identification of patterns in methodological approaches and thematic areas, strengthen the proposal.

However, I believe the manuscript would benefit from major revisions to strengthen methodological transparency, update and expand the literature, and deepen the analytical synthesis of the findings. My main observations are as follows:

I confirm that I have read this submission and believe that I have an appropriate level of expertise to confirm that it is of an acceptable scientific standard, however I have significant reservations, as outlined above.

The authors performed a systematic review to study the effectiveness of exercise or physical activity interventions as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy in treatment-resistant and non-remitted depression. Although the topic is of interest to the scientific community, the article has several major shortcomings that need to be addressed before Indexing can be considered.

General Remarks

Please clarify ambiguous statements (e.g., page 3, line 3; page 4, outcome parameter), and use clear and concise language (e.g., page 3, line 6).

Introduction

The relevance of exercise or physical activity as an add-on therapy for NRD or TRD is not well developed. The authors should explain why exercise could be a good add-on treatment for NRD and TRD. They could use the available evidence showing that exercise is effective for MDD (e.g., Noetel et al., 2024; Morres et al., 2019) to argue that it might also be effective for NRD and TRD, but no systematic review has been conducted so far. Additionally, it would be useful to define physical activity and exercise, and elaborate on the different exercise protocols and how they relate to the current evidence. Finally, the study by Krogh et al. (2017) did not include patients with TRD and NRD.

Methods

Intervention: Please elaborate on the types of interventions included in this review. What kinds of interventions were included? Supervised exercise treatment, activity tracker or online modules, exercise advice, single exercise sessions, etc.?

Comparator: What kinds of control conditions were included?

Outcome: Other outcomes that the authors discuss later should be mentioned here.

Study Design: Include within-person designs. However, it is unclear why the authors chose within-person designs if they only included RCTs.

Quality Appraisal: The quality appraisal is not appropriate. I recommend using other quality assessment tools (e.g., Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool).

Selection of Studies: A table summarizing the selected studies should be included in the manuscript, not in the supplements.

Results

Characteristics of Studies: The provided citations are confusing. The authors state that eight of the studies are from the same project but cite all 11 studies afterward. Only those studies from the same project should be cited here. The same applies to the rest of this paragraph. The authors state that two studies (i.e., Carta and Mather) used concurrent exercise interventions and the others used “traditional” interventions, again citing Carta and Mather. Moreover, "concurrent" and "traditional" interventions are not appropriate terms in this context.

Characteristics of Exercise Interventions: “The period of assessment,” where the authors refer to the assessment of depressive symptoms, should be stated elsewhere. Instead, the intervention period should be mentioned here.

Meta-Analysis Statement: The statement explaining why the authors do not perform a meta-analysis is misplaced in the methods section. Please avoid using informal language.

Discussion

Since eight of the 11 studies used the same population, there are actually only three studies showing that exercise can be an effective add-on treatment to reduce depressive symptoms in TRD and NRD. The amount of evidence is therefore very limited, which the authors should discuss. A more hesitant optimism towards exercise as an add-on treatment for TRD and NRD would be more appropriate considering the limited evidence so far.
